RagShortTexts: The Miracle of Bolsena established Corpus Christi, celebrated with golden monstrance.

Variants.Content: Pope Urban IV promulgated the Feast of Corpus Christi after the Miracle of Bolsena in 1263, when a doubting Bohemian priest saw consecrated communion hosts bleed onto the altar corporal. The feast celebrated the Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist, and Thomas Aquinas composed its liturgy and hymns, among them the Pange Lingua. Cities soon adopted solemn processions in which the consecrated host, displayed in a golden monstrance, was carried through the streets. Guilds marched behind their banners, and the civic processions gave every urban community a public way to show its devotion and its unity.
Corpus Christi united civic guilds and church orders. Walking behind the Blessed Sacrament in ranked hierarchy with beeswax tapers, towns displayed communal solidarity and doctrinal devotion.
Streets are strewn with fresh sweet-rushes and rose petals. When the bishop elevates the radiant golden monstrance under a silk canopy, thousands drop to their knees in awe.
